tasks.short: Show patients how to insert and remove contact lenses, watch them practise until they manage safely, and record the instruction in the patient record.

steps.what: Ophthalmic technician shows patients how to insert or remove contact lenses
Ophthalmic technician watches the patient practise until they manage safely
Ophthalmic technician records the lens instruction in the patient record as free text

tasks.design: The record ({OTHER}) gets a short checklist for lens instruction (insertion, removal, hygiene, wearing schedule, patient manages alone), so the technician ticks items instead of writing a free-text note. Showing the patient and judging when they manage safely stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: The instruction was noted in free text after each session.
tasks.still_hard: Patients who struggle need notes the checklist does not cover.
tasks.human_edge: Calming a patient who flinches at touching their eye.

reach.learn: Whether the instruction given is clear in the record.

evidence.claim: Patient records can hold configurable checklists for routine instruction.
Medical records are kept and shared only with consent; fax is not used for sharing.

assumptions: Boundary: from the lens fitted to the instruction recorded; the lens fitting is outside.
Input contract: checklist set up in the record; fallback is a free-text note.
Instruction at the chair does not change.
research_questions: Is the checklist complete for most patients?

incremental.description: Ophthalmic technician adds a note for patients who struggle.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many patients who struggle; high: mostly routine instruction.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Talk with the patient about needs and style, help them try frames, look up frame stock and prices, and record the chosen frame on the order.

steps.what: Ophthalmic technician talks with patients about their eyewear needs and style
Ophthalmic technician assists patients to select eyewear by trying frames
Ophthalmic technician looks up frame stock and prices on a printed list
Ophthalmic technician writes the chosen frame on the order form

tasks.design: Frames carry a barcode, and the clinic's optical system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) shows stock and price on a scan instead of a printed list. Scanning the chosen frame adds it to the order with the prescription already filled in, so the technician does not write it out. Talking with the patient and helping them choose stay with the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock and prices were read from a printed list and orders written by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Optical systems hold barcoded frame stock and build orders by scan.
tasks.still_hard: Frames from small suppliers come without barcodes.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which frame suits a patient's face and daily life.

evidence.claim: Optical systems can hold barcoded frame stock with prices and build orders by scan.

assumptions: Boundary: from the prescription to the frame recorded; lens ordering is outside.
Input contract: frames barcoded on arrival; fallback is the printed list.
Helping patients choose does not change.
research_questions: Do order errors on frames fall?

incremental.description: Ophthalmic technician labels frames that arrive without barcodes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many unlabelled frames; high: all frames barcoded.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The ophthalmic technician keeps teaching lens handling and helping patients choose eyewear; free-text notes, printed lists and handwritten orders shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A technician with more time for patients.
